about: Voice-cursor calibration / feasibility spec, v2 (wiki/voice-cursor.md). ONE source of truth for the steps, the analysis settings and the per-person rules: the desktop test (extractor/voice_cursor_test.py), its scorer, and later the app's calibration all read this file. Everything is relative to the person. v2 over v1: the range top comes from the glides (capped by the held note), the person accepts or redoes the range on a live meter, levels are measured twice (blind, then with the live pitch meter), vowel takes are scored by their MEASURED pitch band, and the formant tracker keeps broad back-vowel F2s and refuses one-frame jumps to F3. voice_cursor_v1.json stays as it was, so v1 sessions still score the same.

analysis.hpf_note: 2nd-order high-pass before everything: breath and handling thumps on the mic are almost all below 70 Hz (they started and ended v1 takes before the voice came)
analysis.f2_note: F2 may be broad (back rounded vowels on a room mic: 500-1000 Hz); a frame whose F2 is more than f2_jump_hz from the last accepted F2 is dropped (nan) unless f2_jump_frames frames in a row agree, so one lost F2 no longer turns into F3
analysis.smooth_note: pitch and formants are averaged over >= one vibrato cycle (vibrato is 5-7 Hz, so 143-200 ms) before any steadiness test

live.note: the live take loop: a take starts when voice (clarity >= clarity_min, level >= pre-take level + level_over_floor_db) is heard for voiced_ticks_to_start ticks, and stops after take.silence_s without voice; a thump alone never starts or stops a take

intro: Your comfortable pitch range: first two slow glides on an open “ah”, low to high,
then hold your lowest and your highest note you could hold for a while WITHOUT straining.
Comfortable, not extreme, and in your normal voice (no falsetto): this becomes the top and
bottom of the screen. You'll see the result and can redo it.
Your “home note”: the note you hum most easily, without thinking. Hum it 3 times, about 2 s each.
It is the middle of your screen, and in daily use a 3 s home note re-centres your range.
BLIND: five heights, like a staircase: 1 = your comfortable low end, 3 = your home note,
5 = your comfortable high end, 2 and 4 halfway between. Start from silence and go straight
to that height, no warm-up slide, and hold it about 1.5 s. The pitch meter is HIDDEN on
purpose: this measures whether the same note lands on the same spot without looking.
WITH THE METER: the same five heights, but now you see your pitch live on the meter.
The target line is highlighted; get the dot onto it and hold it there until it turns
green (about 0.3 s), then stop. This measures how fast and how exactly you get there.
Hold a vowel, mouth open, for about 2 s at the height shown on the meter: LOW = near your
low end, HOME = your home note, HIGH = near your high end. Keep the vowel clean and steady.
If the pitch lands in another band the take is flagged and you can redo it (r).

steps.sub: about 2 s, normal voice, no straining, no falsetto
Enter = use it    r = redo range and home note

steps.pos_note: pos is the place on the person's own low..home..high scale: 0 = low, 0.5 = home, 1 = high (piecewise, so an off-centre home note is fine)

steps.sub: {stairs}   get the dot onto the line, hold till green

range.rule: top = min(glide top, held high note); bottom = max(glide bottom, held low note); glide top/bottom = the glide_top_pct / glide_bottom_pct percentile of STEADY glide frames (voiced, smoothed pitch moving < glide_max_step_st per hop, so cracks and octave jumps drop out). With no usable glide, the held notes alone. Flag an anchor that lies more than anchor_glide_flag_st beyond the glide edge (falsetto or a strain note): it is not used.

rules.vowel_band_note: a vowel take counts in the band whose pos is nearest to its MEASURED pitch on the person's scale, not the band it was prompted for; live, a mismatch is flagged and offered for a redo
rules.rows: floor(range_st / (rows_sd_factor * sd)), capped at max_rows. rows_blind: sd = pooled repeat SD of the blind levels (same note from silence, no meter). rows_feedback: sd = RMS error of the final pitch from the target over the feedback takes that reached it

feedback.time_to_target: ms from voice onset to the end of the first lock_window_ms in which the smoothed pitch stays within ±lock_pitch_st of the target
feedback.final_note: final accuracy = median smoothed pitch of the last final_ms of the steady part, minus the target (st)
feedback.overshoot: the furthest the smoothed pitch goes past the target (in the direction of approach from the onset pitch) before the lock, st; 0 if it never passes

rules.columns: per pitch band: 'vowel' (3 columns: oo left, ah centre, ee right) if that band's leave-one-take-out vowel accuracy >= vowel_acc_min, else 'snap' (height picks a screen band, short hums step through the tappable elements in it)

go.why: the position cursor always shows its dot, so the go/no-go uses the with-meter measurement; the blind rows only say whether you could also jump without looking

rules.verdict: GO if rows_feedback >= rows_feedback_min and time-to-target p90 <= time_to_target_p90_max_ms and never-reached <= never_reached_max_frac, and at least one band uses 'vowel'; SNAP-ONLY if the same but every band snaps; NO-GO otherwise. Reported with it: 'absolute (no look) too' if rows_blind >= blind_rows_absolute_min
